growth_signal.value: Raised a $30M Series A in October 2026, after a pre-seed in September 2025.

raised.value: $38.5M total, including a $30M Series A led by Oak HC/FT (Oct 2026)

entry.idea: AI agents are good at maths and code but weak at real office work like building a financial model, so Halluminate builds practice workplaces and tests where AI can learn and be graded on that work.
entry.lesson: When everyone sells the same shovels, sell the training ground: build realistic practice worlds with a clear way to score the result.
entry.name: Halluminate

growth.basis: substitute: funding round bigger than the last ($30M Series A after a pre-seed)
growth.reason: A much bigger round than its first one and top investors joining, but no revenue or customer numbers.

market.reason: Every AI lab and many firms building work agents could need training environments, starting with finance.

tech.reason: Realistic work simulations with expert-made tasks and real deal data are hard work, but a good team could copy the approach.

entry.twist: Its practice workplaces copy a real job, with an inbox, a data room of files, tools and coworkers, and its tests use anonymised papers from real private deals.
entry.who_pays: AI labs and companies that build AI agents pay for the training environments and benchmarks.
entry.why_now: AI labs have used up easy training data and now need realistic, checkable work tasks to make agents useful in jobs like finance.

mentions.snippet: Training environments and benchmarks for financial AI; $30M Series A
San Francisco startup providing sandboxes and datasets to train computer and browser use agents. Backed by Y Combinator. Pre-seed, September 2025.
mentions.title: Halluminate
